findings.description: SATISFIED, and re-proven by mutation. Both cases are asserted and both discriminate. Case 1 (planted lint defect): I built the scope by hand (old-only copy, link appended, Tier 1 --apply, committed, then an unknown key planted) and the shipped script exited 1 reporting 'lint failures: 1' plus a named FAIL naming frontmatter-known-keys and `bogus_key`; suite 1123-1132 asserts exactly that. Case 2 (aborting lint): running verify-migration.sh from a copied scripts/ dir whose lint-scope.sh is a stub exiting 2 produced 'verify-lint: lint-scope.sh aborted with exit status 2 before printing a summary' and 'lint failures: unknown (aborted before a summary)' at exit 1 -- never 'lint failures: 0'. That the stub ran at all proves the sibling resolution via dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" (verify-migration.sh:96), since the real lint passes that clean scope. The abort assertion genuinely discriminates: MUTANT-C (exit status ignored, summary grepped instead, abort treated as clean) made the suite exit 1 at 'verify-migration.sh exited zero against an aborting lint'. The yq preflight is present and fires on this script's own terms: with yq off PATH the run printed 'yq is required and not on PATH (brew install yq)' and exited 2 before reaching the lint (verify-migration.sh:70-73).

Manual case 2 via copied scripts/: 'FAIL ...: verify-lint: lint-scope.sh aborted with exit status 2 before printing a summary' / 'lint failures: unknown (aborted before a summary)' / exit=1. yq removed from PATH: 'yq is required and not on PATH (brew install yq)' / exit=2. MUTANT-C (grep-based lint) suite exit=1, stderr 'verify-migration.sh exited zero against an aborting lint'.

findings.description: SATISFIED, no regression from r0. The script reads git diff --name-status -M "$since_ref" (verify-migration.sh:191) and never git status --porcelain. I built a committed-migration combo scope by hand and confirmed porcelain reports 0 lines on it (the exact case the clause's failing example names), while the shipped script reports 'renames: 1', 'deletions: 1', 'failures: 3' with renames and deletions named as separate FAIL lines under the verify-rename diagnostic. MUTANT-P (the rename loop fed from git status --porcelain) on the same hand-built scope reports 'renames: 0 / deletions: 0 / failures: 1' and emits no verify-rename line at all, so suite assertions 1065, 1066 and 1067 each discriminate a porcelain implementation. Run against the full suite, MUTANT-P exits 1.

findings.description: SATISFIED, no regression from r0. Byte-identity is asserted across two failing runs by hashing every file under the scope (hash_scope at 952-954 shells out to shasum over find -type f, excluding .git) before and after: the combo run at 1051-1053/1060-1063 and the lint-defect run at 1119-1121/1127-1130. I reproduced it independently on my own combo scope -- the 4-file hash set was identical before and after a failing run. The multi-failure requirement is exceeded rather than merely met: the combo scope carries three planted defects and the suite asserts all three FAIL lines plus 'failures: 3', which my own run reproduced (three FAIL lines printed, not just the first). A source scan for write-capable operations across the whole script turns up nothing: every redirection is to >&2 or /dev/null, and there is no mv, rm, cp, sed -i, tee, touch or mkdir anywhere.

findings.description: SATISFIED for what this task added or revised; the record paragraph's final prose is T-004's and is not judged here. Every one of the nine comment blocks in verify-migration.sh explains why the code has the shape it does, and none restates the next line: the header names the constraint that forces a git-history read over a working-tree read ('by the time anyone runs this, --apply is long finished and git status on a committed change reports a clean tree'); line 68 explains why the yq preflight lives here rather than in the lint ('before ever reaching a sibling that would otherwise take the blame'); 93-95 and 104-108 each name the trap being avoided rather than the mechanism; 142 justifies skipping template placeholders; 171-173 names porcelain's specific blind spot. Scans for the humanizer tells the rubric calls out come back clean: no promotional framing (seamless/robust/powerful/ensures/leverage/comprehensive and the rest all return no hits), no bolded inline headers in comments, no em dashes at all so the spacing rule cannot be violated, and no rule-of-three padding -- the one enumeration, 'bash, awk, git, and yq', is a factual four. The voice matches the neighbors, which open with a one-sentence what and then explain the shape's rationale (lint-scope.sh:1-12, migrate-scope.sh:1-14). Failure strings follow the house fail() idiom exactly, 'FAIL <scope>: <diagnostic>: <message>' against lint-scope.sh:74-77, and the report block reuses the neighbors' 'failures: N' summary shape.
